A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Do-PFN research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, revised, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic CID and CATE experiments, Amazon Sales and Law School evaluations, and robustness, calibration, and bias analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds ATE evaluation, RealCause experiments, distribution-shift tests, and inference-speed measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the transformer architecture and treatment indicator, negative-log-likelihood training, and CATE computation remain unchanged. Although xpt becomes xin, Appendix C still samples covariates before intervention using shared noise. The new Do-PFN v1.1 variant changes training scale and graph-size support, rather than introducing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds four RealCause groups—ACIC 2016, IHDP, Lalonde CPS, and Lalonde PSID—providing realistic semi-synthetic CATE scenarios satisfying unconfoundedness. It also adds ATE evaluation and test scenarios with unfamiliar noise distributions, mechanisms, and larger graphs. The original synthetic and known-graph datasets remain, although known-graph CID reporting and the observational-regression diagnostic are removed.

E2.justification: The synthetic CATE comparison adds TARNet, DragonNet, and T-Learner (TabPFN), beyond v1 Figure 4's comparator set. Known-graph comparisons also add neural and hyperparameter-optimized learners (v2 Figure 6). Existing TabPFN-CATE S/X/DML comparators are retained under renamed labels; Do-PFN-Short is removed from the Common Effect comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a 96-hour variant trained on graphs up to 60 nodes, ATE relative-error evaluation, timed RealCause comparisons, and controlled OOD settings. Appendix E.1 specifies up to 100 RealCause realizations per group and up to 10,000 samples. The original model's appendix training time changes from 40 to 48 hours, matching v1's main text; this correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds explicit OOD tests of noise distributions, nonlinear mechanisms, and graph size, plus speed–accuracy analysis on RealCause. Existing calibration and bias analyses are retained and relocated. The separate sufficiency stratification, observational-regression comparison, and Amazon/Law School prediction scatterplots from v1 are removed.

E5.justification: v1 already reports confidence intervals, Nemenyi comparisons, critical-difference diagrams, and calibration variability. v2 Appendix E.6 additionally specifies a Friedman test preceding Nemenyi comparisons and the significance threshold alpha = 0.05. This expands statistical documentation without establishing increased runs or seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for ATE, RealCause, OOD behavior, and runtime. It reports competitive v1.1 performance on three of four RealCause groups, Pareto-front membership across all four, and degradation under doubled Gaussian variance and averaged nonlinearities. Figure 4 also reports better large-graph performance for the differently trained v1.1 model; this is not a same-configuration improvement over v1.pdf.

T1.justification: The original Proposition 1 and proof remain. v2 adds a posterior-predictive formulation and Proposition 2 in Appendix A.1, an uncertainty decomposition in Section 3, and observational-equivalence definitions, assumptions, and a claimed consistency theorem with a Doob-based proof in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The core claim of causal prediction without a supplied graph is retained. v2 elevates uncertainty decomposition and asymptotic consistency to explicit theoretical contributions, whereas v1 advertised the prior-relative optimality result. Its conclusion additionally claims robustness beyond the training prior and distinguishes competitive unconfounded performance from stronger performance in mediated settings.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a three-source interpretation of predictive uncertainty and discusses which uncertainty should persist asymptotically. It adds explanations involving calibration error, the prior's preference for small treatment effects, and RealCause's enforced unconfoundedness. Conversely, v1's discussion of trust and interpretability, including speculative graph-discovery-then-adjustment reasoning, is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds EconML/CATENets implementation information, 60-second FLAML tuning budgets, and training specifications for additional variants. Appendix D.4 clarifies known-graph simulation, and the checklist explicitly states availability of inference code and raw results. The underlying prior-generation recipe, architecture description, and GPU specification largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2's research positioning is largely retained. Added references support RealCause, neural baselines, tuning software, and the new theory; Appendix B acknowledges ideas from Balazadeh et al.'s CausalPFN consistency argument. The earlier Zhang et al. discussion and reference are removed.

P1.justification: The contribution list, experimental narrative, and discussion are substantially rewritten. Ablations and hybrid-data sections exchange order, dataset descriptions move into Appendix D.4, and supplementary results are reorganized into thematic sections. Terminology is standardized around Do-PFN version labels, and a conference checklist is appended.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout and combines synthetic CID/CATE displays with a new ATE row in Figure 3. Critical-difference diagrams move into a separate appendix section; OOD, RealCause, and speed figures are added, and known-graph comparisons are redesigned. Earlier scatterplots disappear, while retained calibration, bias, and graph figures are resized or rearranged.

improvement.justification: RealCause, stronger baselines, OOD tests, and speed comparisons materially strengthen v1's empirical validation. However, the new central theoretical contribution has an unresolved conditioning gap: Equations (12)–(13) switch between p(psi|Dob) and p(psi|Dob,xin), and Appendix B drops query-covariate conditioning without justification from Algorithm 1. The empirical gains therefore coexist with weakened confidence in the enlarged theoretical claims, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
